name: Centrist Marxism
summary: Centrist Marxism holds a middle course between revolutionary communism and reformist social democracy. It keeps the Marxist analysis of class struggle and the goal of socialising production, but insists that the working class win power through democracy, parliament and mass organisation, and it rejects Bolshevik dictatorship and vanguard rule.
scope: Represents the democratic centre of the Second International as developed by Karl Kautsky (Erfurt Programme commentary, The Dictatorship of the Proletariat, USPD) and the Austromarxists around Otto Bauer, with the Two-and-a-half International. Excludes Leninism and revisionist reformism, and treats later left socialists such as the ILP and POUM only as fellow travellers.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Kautsky's Marxism holds that capitalist markets generate crises and class exploitation and that land and industry must ultimately be socialized.

public-ownership.rationale: Kautsky held that land and the large means of production must ultimately be socialized, and public ownership of major industry is the standard Erfurt-style demand.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Reform measures pursued within parliament while awaiting revolution would include progressive taxation, though the sources name no specific tax policy.

unions-good.rationale: Kautsky's strategy centred on organising workers into party and unions and wearing down opponents, so organised labour is central.

property-fundamental.rationale: Centrist Marxists see private ownership of the means of production as the root of class rule and expect it to be socialized.

cut-welfare.rationale: Austromarxist Red Vienna expanded housing, health and education, and a workers' movement sees welfare as a gain of the working class.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialization of industry was the goal, but Kautsky-style Marxism stressed public or social ownership more than worker-run firms, and adherents differ on the form.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Kautsky defended freedom of press and association for all parties, which cuts against speech limits, while anti-racist socialists could favour them.

strong-leader.rationale: Kautsky rejected personal or party rule outside democratic majority control and saw dictatorship as opening the way to the dictatorship of the sword.

state-harmful.rationale: Centrist Marxists want to conquer and use the democratic state, not abolish it; Kautsky's dictatorship concerns rule on the basis of democracy.

decide-locally.rationale: Austromarxists worked for national and municipal self-government in Red Vienna yet pursued central economic transformation, so local primacy is not their stance.

traditional-family.rationale: Kautsky's materialism and anti-clericalism made him critical of inherited tradition, though the family question is not covered in the sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: Kautsky was anti-Christian and materialist, and the movement's tradition is secular and hostile to clerical influence.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Kautsky denounced colonial policy as racist and exploitative, from which support for correcting racial injustice follows, though the statement is modern.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Bauer held national identity compatible with class consciousness and defended national culture as a community of character, but the tradition is internationalist.

gradual-change.rationale: Centrists accepted reform in the meantime but still held that a socialist revolution must come, so they reject gradualism that merely respects established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Internationalist workers' parties opposed chauvinism, though trade unions sometimes worried about labour competition.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about other international bodies (such as the EU, WTO, IMF or WHO) or about support, funding or reform without enforcement powers, and the statement now asks whether the UN should have powers to enforce its decisions against member states.

reviewHistory.rationale: The tradition built the Two-and-a-half International and the later Labour and Socialist International for coordination, and Kautsky wanted international cooperation, such as the ultra-imperialist hope.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about other international bodies (such as the EU, WTO, IMF or WHO) or about support, funding or reform without enforcement powers, and the statement now asks whether the UN should have powers to enforce its decisions against member states.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

free-trade.rationale: Kautsky saw capitalist trade as an arena of finance-capital rivalry; he did not endorse the claim that free trade benefits everyone.

nation-first.rationale: Kautsky condemned the SPD's war truce and chauvinism and the tradition is internationalist.

open-borders.rationale: Internationalist in spirit, but the sources are silent on borders, and adherents split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Marxists held that technology creates the material basis for socialism but that social relations decide its use.

revolution-justified.rationale: Centrists support revolution at some future point while using reform now, though Kautsky stressed democratic means and called for defence of democracy against force.

experts-over-public.rationale: Austromarxists rejected the vanguard and held that consciousness should arise from workers' own awakening, which cuts against rule by experts.

land-value-tax.rationale: Kautsky held that land must ultimately be socialized rather than taxed as a substitute for other taxes.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Kautsky was sceptical of nationalist economic policy, though social-democratic parties sometimes accepted protection.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Kautsky argued large-scale production is superior in agriculture and industry, and the programme aimed at social ownership, not wide small property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about abolishing wage labour, not money, and the statement now asks only about money; wage labour has its own statement.

reviewHistory.rationale: Marxism sees wage labour as a feature of capitalism to be superseded eventually, but centrists did not emphasise this.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about abolishing wage labour, not money, and the statement now asks only about money; wage labour has its own statement.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A tradition seeking democratic control of the economy and socialised finance would not hand money to the market; Kautsky saw finance capital as a power to be curbed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Kautsky's strategy rested on independent class organisation and class struggle, not state-recognised partnership bodies that fix wages and prices. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

one-party-rule.rationale: Kautsky condemned Bolshevik single-party dictatorship and held that every party keeps the right to strive to become the majority.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Kautsky wanted a democratic republic, and the Austromarxists and SPD fought hereditary privilege.

democracy-best.rationale: Kautsky wrote that there is no socialism without democracy and that the proletariat must defend it with tooth and nail.

workers-councils.rationale: After 1918 Kautsky favoured a National Assembly over council rule, though some centrists such as Adler saw a role for councils.

natural-rulers.rationale: Kautsky rejected tutelage and rule over the working class by any elite, and defended equal democratic rights.

political-violence-never.rationale: Centrists supported revolution in principle and defence of democracy against force, so they do not hold that political violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Kautsky opposed the SPD's war truce and sought to reconquer peace, and the tradition does not glorify war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Kautsky's anti-clerical materialism and the secular democratic programme favour separation, though the sources do not quote a programme demand. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A secular, anti-Christian materialist tradition grounds law in democratic decision.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Marxists regard courts and force as functions of a public, democratically controlled state.

military-superiority.rationale: Kautsky opposed annexationist war aims and imperial rivalry.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Bauer defined the nation as a community of character and destiny and built non-territorial minority protections, not ethnic homogeneity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Kautsky's orthodox Marxism, expressed in The Class Struggle, treats class conflict as the main driver of history.

civilizational-union.rationale: The tradition is class-based and internationalist, not built around civilisational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: A socialist tradition prizes solidarity and collective emancipation over self-interest as a moral basis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Kautsky's emphasis on democratic freedoms and equal rights puts the individual's rights prominently, though solidarity matters.

limit-population.rationale: Marxists attribute poverty to social institutions rather than population and would not endorse coercive limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The tradition holds that capitalist industry builds the material basis for socialism, not that it is a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Marxists see technology as creating the basis for socialism but Kautsky argued revolution cannot be forced early.

restore-past-order.rationale: A Marxist tradition expecting socialism as the next stage after capitalism puts progress ahead of restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Kautsky defended an orthodox Marxist theory as guide to strategy, though he was also pragmatic about timing.

direct-action.rationale: Kautsky's strategy was organising workers and winning reforms through parliamentary democracy, not extra-parliamentary direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Kautsky argued that socialism could only be reached by democratic means, since proletarian rule must rest on democracy.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Marxist progress theory treats the productive forces as the basis for a better society, not a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Kautsky stressed the superiority of large-scale organised production, and the Marxist long-term ideal of abolishing the division of labour was not a centrist demand.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialisation of production aims to replace production for profit, which is the Erfurt-programme premise.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Kautsky's Class Struggle summary of Marx treats profit as surplus drawn from wage labour.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Kautsky read Marx's dictatorship as a condition of working-class rule on the basis of democracy, and rejected dictatorship as a form of government that disenfranchises opponents.

collective-farming.rationale: Kautsky wanted to win the agricultural proletariat and neutralise small peasants and eventually socialise land, but opposed forcing collectivisation on peasants.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Kautsky split from Lenin by treating imperialism as a policy of finance capital rather than an inevitable stage and conjectured ultra-imperialism, while Bauer saw imperialism as an inevitable product of capital. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

taxation-theft.rationale: A Marxist party seeking taxation and social provision rejects the libertarian claim.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Bauer's nation-as-community and personal principle for national minorities give group dimensions to rights.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Kautsky held that democratic participation and the vote are essential: no socialism without democracy.

state-as-business.rationale: The tradition opposes treating public life as a market and holds that the state must serve the working class on a democratic basis.

positive-liberty.rationale: A tradition aimed at socialising ownership holds that formal liberty means little without the material means to act.

media-academia-power.rationale: Centrists would say economic power controls media and politics, not universities, though Kautsky does not discuss this.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Kautsky called colonial policy racist and held a materialist view of society, and the tradition rejects racial determinism.

organic-representation.rationale: Kautsky championed parliamentary democracy on the basis of universal suffrage over corporate or family representation.

total-state.rationale: Kautsky contrasted socialism with systems of tutelage that are intolerable to modern people and insisted on democratic freedoms.

national-rebirth.rationale: The tradition is internationalist and class-based and rejects national rebirth as a political goal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Kautsky opposed the SPD's annexationist war aims and condemned colonial policy as exploitative.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on democratic majority rule in this tradition, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Kautsky wanted to win the agricultural proletariat and socialise land, and feudal bondage is incompatible with that.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxists see ideology as shaped by class interests, but Kautsky's scientific materialism holds that science is knowable.

universal-morality.rationale: Kautsky traced ethics to natural origins through Darwin, which cuts against fixed universals, but also held democratic and humanist values.

single-common-good.rationale: Class struggle theory holds that classes have opposed interests, so there is no one common good under capitalism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Rejecting vanguard rule and aiming at social ownership and democratic control, Austromarxists favoured democratic workers' say, though they emphasised party and state over firm-level councils.

school-vouchers.rationale: Red Vienna expanded public education, and a Marxist party favours state-provided schooling.

economic-freedom.rationale: Marxists hold that capitalist economic freedom is class power and that political freedom needs democracy and socialisation.

rule-by-example.rationale: Kautsky grounded politics on democratic institutions and law, not on the moral example of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Kautsky's Liberation of Nations (1917) treated national self-determination as part of democracy, but Bauer and Renner, also in scope, proposed non-territorial cultural autonomy for nations inside a multinational state rather than a state for each nation; the strands differ.

force-without-un.rationale: Kautsky opposed aggressive war and only legitimated national self-defence.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Kautsky was an anti-Christian materialist, though the statement's absoluteness leaves room for hedging.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Internationalist workers' movements resist dividing workers by nationality.

class-collaboration.rationale: Kautsky opposed the SPD's Burgfrieden and held that class struggle was the heart of Marxism.

workers-nation.rationale: Kautsky and the centrists upheld the international working class against the SPD's wartime nationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Marxist tradition supports equal rights for women and rejects legally defined roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Marxists criticise finance capital but did not propose banning interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Kautsky denounced colonial rule as racist, and the tradition holds the equality of persons.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Centrists accept the Marxist view of the state as class rule but, with Kautsky, hold that a democratic republic could serve the proletariat.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Bauer's cultural-autonomy approach to nations favoured protecting minority communities over forced assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in Marxist materialist analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: Austrian and German social democrats favoured proportional systems, and Kautsky's democratic majoritarianism supports fair representation, though the sources are not explicit. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

national-mission.rationale: Internationalists reject national missions; Kautsky condemned colonial policy and annexation.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Marxists see parties as class instruments, but centrists defended parliamentary democracy and did not hold this as a general claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Racial and eugenic state coercion conflicts with the democratic and humanist stance.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Centrists wanted the democratic state to socialise major industry and provide welfare.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Kautsky denounced racism, and the tradition holds the equality of people.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Kautsky's democratic socialism rests on equal rights and rejects tutelage and class privilege.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Bauer rejected armed revolution in Austria in part because it could not defend itself against intervention, but the centrists did not clearly hold that socialism cannot last in one country.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A secular, equal-citizenship tradition favours uniform civil law, though Bauer's cultural autonomy allowed nations to run cultural matters.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Secular democrats defend individual freedom of conscience.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious prohibition imposed by law is opposed by a secular materialist tradition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Kautsky was anti-Christian and the tradition favoured secular education, though Austrian practice was contested.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Kautsky rejected the Bolshevik dictatorship and held that socialism requires democracy; no strengthening of the state against it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Kautsky argued that socialism cannot be reached without democracy and majority rule.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade aims are not part of the tradition.

population-transfer.rationale: Kautsky stood for democratic self-determination and condemned chauvinism; Bauer protected minorities by cultural autonomy.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The centrists accepted revolution at some point and defence of democracy against force, so the absolute libertarian position is not theirs.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Marxists see class conflict, not Social Darwinist struggle between peoples, as the engine, and Kautsky condemned chauvinism.

separated-powers.rationale: Kautsky favoured parliamentary democracy as the vehicle of working-class power rather than checks that block majorities, so he is neither clearly for nor against.

vanguard-party.rationale: Austromarxists rejected the party vanguard and held that class consciousness grows from the working class's own awakening.

priority-to-poor.rationale: A workers' movement prioritises the needs of the working class, though framed as class rather than charity.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Red Vienna's municipal housing was a public good, so selling it off conflicts with the model.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: A labour-based tradition defends the right to strike.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxists attribute poverty to social institutions and class relations, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Bauer's nationalities programme sought coexistence of national communities, and the tradition rejects ethnic homogeneity as a precondition.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Kautsky advocated election in a parliamentary democracy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Kautsky insisted on press freedom and rights even under pressure and warned against dictatorship, though he accepted defending democracy.

party-controls-media.rationale: Kautsky opposed suppressing press freedom and called it part of democracy.

party-commands-army.rationale: Bauer wanted the military democratised and under democratic control, not a party's command.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Internationalist workers' movements favoured easier access to citizenship.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The Paris Commune model Kautsky cited had officials on workmen's wages, though the sources do not stress it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Kautsky defended a disciplined, organised party as central to strategy, though without Leninist centralism.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Kautsky sought international cooperation and ultra-imperialism's peaceful cartels, and later socialists backed European integration.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Kautsky's model is a parliamentary republic with the legislature supreme.

clerical-rule.rationale: Kautsky was anti-Christian and the tradition is secular and democratic.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Kautsky urged abstention on war credits and opposed the truce but did not call for defeat of one's own government, unlike Lenin.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Kautsky defended freedom of press and expression.

recall-officials.rationale: Commune-style accountability was part of Marx's account that Kautsky cited, though recall is not stressed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Red Vienna built municipal rental housing rather than universal ownership.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Kautsky argued that large-scale production was superior and focused on the proletariat rather than romanticising rural life.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The tradition valued education and Kautsky was himself an intellectual leader.

death-penalty.rationale: Social democracy opposed the death penalty; sources are silent.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Bauer's nation was a community of destiny not defined by blood, and the tradition favours inclusive citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Bauer's national-cultural autonomy and the personal principle protected minority cultural institutions and schools.

constituent-assembly.rationale: After 1918 Kautsky favoured a democratic republic and a National Assembly over council rule.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Kautsky rejected suspending democratic freedoms and called universal suffrage too valuable to discard.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Kautsky opposed annexation and chauvinism, and territorial claims are not placed above peace.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The tradition holds that private property in the means of production should be socialized for social benefit.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Kautsky opposed annexations and upheld self-determination.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Kautsky's materialism and democratic republicanism reject divine monarchy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A workers' party favours progressive taxation.

character-from-environment.rationale: Kautsky's materialism and Darwin-informed ethics treat character as shaped by social conditions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Kautsky rejected arbitrary rule and tutelage, and defended democracy.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Democratic majority rule is the aim, not mixed rule by the few and the many.

leader-cult.rationale: Kautsky rejected personal rule and dictatorship, which he saw as leading to the dictatorship of the sword.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Kautsky held that the proletariat's rule rests on democracy and did not frame party leaders as restorers of capital.

land-redistribution.rationale: Kautsky argued land must eventually be socialized, not given to small farmers, and opposed an agrarian program defending small peasants.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Kautsky and Bauer opposed ethnic irredentism, and Bauer's nation was non-territorial.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: A secular tradition defends freedom of conscience.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The tradition is class-based and internationalist, not organised by ancestry.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Bauer and Renner's personal principle gave national minorities self-governing cultural associations.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Poale Zion belonged to the centrist internationals while the Bund and Folkspartei took up the personal principle, so adherents are split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Kautsky's orthodox Marxism, as in the Erfurt Programme's theory, treats production relations as the driver of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Kautsky saw cartels as a stage toward ultra-imperialism and eventual socialisation, not something to break up.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Kautsky prized majority rule, but also defended minority rights, so adherents are split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Kautsky opposed colonial exploitation and sought peace through cooperation, rejecting closed blocs.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive structure under socialism was not debated by centrists, who concentrated on how workers could win power democratically.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Kautsky called the October Revolution a premature coup and held that revolution cannot be forced early.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Democratic republic and abolition of class privileges are core.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Kautsky called colonial policy exploitative, brutalising and racist.

patriotic-education.rationale: Internationalists opposed chauvinism and nationalist indoctrination.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation was not a centrist theme, though Kautsky's attention to finance capital leaves open public control.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Kautsky held that socialist revolution was inevitable but could not be forced early, so he saw capitalism's contradictions as persistent while ultra-imperialism was a conjecture.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Leninist thesis, which centrists did not hold; Kautsky stressed unity of workers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Kautsky denounced racism and the tradition holds equal rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Kautsky condemned colonial policy as exploitative, but the legal status of colonial-era treaties is not covered in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Kautsky favoured a democratic republic with universal suffrage.

minority-veto.rationale: Majority rule with minority rights, not minority veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Kautsky called on the working class to defend democracy with tooth and nail, though the statement is framed in constitutional-monarchy terms.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Kautsky held that a parliamentary republic could serve the proletariat and championed democratic parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics did not figure in the centrist tradition, though Kautsky's Darwinian materialism treats humans as part of nature.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The tradition sees class justice, not charity from the privileged, as the remedy.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-style claim not found in the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian claim not found in the sources.

native-born-offices.rationale: Internationalist and equal-rights tradition rejects it.

party-own-road.rationale: Centrists stood between Second and Third Internationals and rejected Moscow's control, as the Two-and-a-half International and POUM show.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries was not a centrist topic, and the sources give no lead.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Kautsky opposed annexationist aims and chauvinism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Kautsky denounced Bolshevik dictatorship, but equating it with fascism is a later thesis, and adherents are split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Kautsky held that democracy is the universal necessity for socialism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Bauer wanted the military taken from the ruling class and made democratic.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligations between adult children and parents are not treated in the sources.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Social insurance and public welfare are central to the tradition.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary democracy was central to Kautsky's strategy.

single-official-language.rationale: Bauer's nationalities programme favoured minority language and cultural rights.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The centrists did not write about consumption, although critics of capitalism often link it to commodity culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Kautsky opposed aggressive war and annexation.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Kautsky condemned the Bolshevik use of force and championed self-determination.

corporate-influence.rationale: Kautsky saw finance capital driving policy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Kautsky emphasised democratic legitimacy and law.

non-intervention.rationale: Kautsky opposed aggressive war and annexation, and defended self-determination.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Kautsky was a materialist who treated antisemitism and racism as ideological, and the tradition rejects conspiracy theories.

local-production.rationale: The tradition favoured large-scale organised production but did not address regional self-sufficiency, so no position emerges.

informal-organisation.rationale: Kautsky stood for a mass organised party.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxists distinguish personal belongings from the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: The tradition is socialist and critiqued Bolshevism from the left, not for defeat.

religion-illusion.rationale: Kautsky was a materialist and anti-Christian, though his writing on this is not detailed in the sources.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Kautsky's orthodox Marxism holds that capitalism develops the productive forces and the proletariat as the material basis for socialism.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Kautsky wanted national and international socialisation of large-scale production, not small communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Bauer's minority protections run against majoritarian settlement policies.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Centrists place themselves between reformism and Bolshevism but aim at socialism, so they do not endorse a third course beyond capitalism and socialism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Kautsky opposed irredentist chauvinism and backed democratic self-determination.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Rejected as a factual matter; Kautsky's family were persecuted by Nazis.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Kautsky held every party retains the right to strive to become the majority.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Kautsky's 1907 pamphlet condemned colonial policy as exploitative.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Austromarxists held that class consciousness grows from workers' own awakening, but their model was parliamentary and party-led, not participatory in a strong sense.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Centrists defined themselves by position between the left and right of the socialist movement.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Opposed as a civilizational generalisation by a materialist, internationalist tradition.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Kautsky grounded authority in democratic majorities.

social-market-economy.rationale: Centrists sought socialisation, but accept reform now, so a permanent social market is not their aim.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Bauer wanted military control democratised, not abolished.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Two-and-a-half International stood between the Second and Third Internationals, but the statement concerns military blocs, so this is an analogy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Democratic republic and abolition of hereditary privilege.

property-franchise.rationale: Kautsky championed universal suffrage and called its abandonment suicide.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Kautsky defended press freedom while a Marxist analysis holds that capital owns media.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Kautsky held that law and democratic procedure should replace arbitrary rule.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition-based bodies are a modern device, and the tradition's commitment to elected parliaments leaves the answer open.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Marxist critique of concentration of capital, though the statement is a candidate and not directly documented.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Kautsky favoured democracy and freedom of conscience, and Austrian and German practice was secular rather than anti-religious.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its own rationale does not support its value under the reworded statement: it describes cultural autonomy, legislative representation or a shared symbol, not shared executive power.

reviewHistory.rationale: Bauer's personal principle of national autonomy is a form of institutional power-sharing between communities, though not executive coalitions.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its own rationale does not support its value under the reworded statement: it describes cultural autonomy, legislative representation or a shared symbol, not shared executive power.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Marxist centrists held that poverty is a structural result of capitalism to be remedied by social provision and socialisation, not philanthropy; Red Vienna built public welfare instead of relying on charity.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The goal of socialising production so that income no longer rests on ownership of capital is a defining aim of centrist Marxism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Marxism holds politics to be material class struggle, not a spiritual struggle between good and evil.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The class-based internationalist tradition and Bauer's national cultural autonomy treat all nationalities as equals, so reserving the economy for the majority is rejected.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Kautsky's case is that the working class must win and hold political power through democracy; a regime that suppresses it is not socialist.

person-over-state.rationale: Kautsky opposed dictatorship over individuals yet aimed at collective ownership; the sources do not settle the statement.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Austromarxists favoured federal nationality autonomy, but the sources do not settle revocability of regional powers.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Austromarxists put class over race and national groups, and Bauer's national-cultural autonomy was not racial.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Austromarxists such as Bauer treated the nation as a cultural community of shared language and fate that cuts across state borders, which is why they proposed national-cultural autonomy.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Kautsky's group opposed war credits in 1914 and the USPD campaigned against the war, though they did not call for mutiny; support is the documented tendency.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The movement stood for strong unions and organised workers bargaining collectively as the base of the working class's democratic power.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Kautsky argued against Lenin that the proletariat should win and use democratic state power rather than smash it, though he accepted deep reform of the state; the Marx-quoting dispute turns on this.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The movement held that socialism needs a planned economy and organised democratic socialisation, not a free-for-all of experiments; it never endorsed a no-blueprint position.

sacred-nation.rationale: Marxism treats the working class as an international class and Kautsky and Bauer opposed nationalism as bourgeois, though Bauer analysed nations as communities; a sacred nation contradicts the core.

workers-own-party.rationale: Centrist Marxism rests on an independent working-class party (the SPD, then the USPD) winning power through democracy.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Kautsky made universal suffrage, majority rule and a free press the test of democracy against Bolshevik rule, though he also wanted democracy to serve socialisation.

premarital-sex.rationale: Sexual morality was not a theme of the sources, and Red Vienna's reformers and traditional socialists differed on it.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Erfurt Programme that Kautsky explained demanded universal suffrage and equal rights for women and men.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Centrists criticised Bolshevik bureaucratic dictatorship yet many, like Bauer, valued the Soviet economic base, so the strand is split.

indirect-election.rationale: Kautsky defended universal suffrage and parliamentary democracy and rejected the soviet council system as a basis of rule.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Bauer's national cultural autonomy and Kautsky's self-determination favour minority self-rule, though Bauer's scheme was mainly personal, not territorial.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Kautsky backed national self-determination, and a vote by the inhabitants is the democratic way to apply it.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Kautsky defended democracy, universal suffrage, press freedom and minority rights against rule by force, which excludes killing without trial.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Kautsky rejected tutelage and vanguard rule and held that socialism comes through democracy, parties and mass organisation.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Kautsky's Marxism treats unequal distribution as the product of class exploitation and requires socialising the means of production, whatever the formal voluntariness of exchange.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Centrist Marxism keeps the Marxist analysis of class and exploitation that Kautsky popularised in his Erfurt Programme commentary, which rests on labour as the source of value.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Centrists rejected single-party communist rule as dictatorship without democracy, which Kautsky argued in his critique of the Bolsheviks.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Austromarxist Red Vienna expanded housing, health and education, and a workers' movement sees welfare as a gain of the working class. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Kautsky rejected colonial policy. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: A socialist government should win office through free elections and leave power if it loses them.
missingStatements.rationale: Kautsky argued that every party reduced to a minority keeps the right to strive to become the majority and that socialism cannot exist without democracy.

missingStatements.text: Democracy should be defended even against attempts to suppress it by force.
missingStatements.rationale: Kautsky said the proletariat should defend democracy with tooth and nail if ruling classes use force against a democratic majority.

notes: Trotskyists use 'centrist' pejoratively; the profile follows Kautsky and the Austromarxists, and the ILP and POUM would differ on some revolutionary points.
